item.title: What makes the dossier strong - and where evidence is still needed
item.lead: The strength of the source lies in the coherence of the hypotheses; its weakness lies in places where interpretation is formulated as an established mechanism.

blocks.text: The repeated attention to backend processes is strong. Instead of merely looking at the visible interface, the dossier asks who manages the account, how data is stored, how labor is distributed, and how payments are processed. These are concrete research questions.
The triangulation concept is also strong. Legal documents, technical artifacts, and sociological data can reinforce each other when they present the same event from different perspectives.

More evidence is required for the most significant causality claims: the relationship between adult-tech and demographic decline, the assumption that societal anxiety is deliberately commercially induced, and the link between specific microtransactions and organized crime. Such claims demand independent datasets and primary sources.
The most credible subsequent version is therefore not necessarily more assertive, but more precise: each claim receives a source status, an evidence requirement, and a falsification criterion.
